findings.title: Negative queryset slice from user-controlled cursor
findings.body: In src/sentry/api/paginator.py OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result allows cursor.offset < 0 to flow directly into queryset[start_offset:stop] when enable_advanced_features is true. Offset comes from the user-supplied cursor string (Cursor.from_string parses int(bits[1]) with no range check). Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing and raise ValueError, so a crafted cursor like 0:-5:0 turns a paginated GET into a 500 instead of a 400, giving any caller who can reach the endpoint a trivial DoS. The comment claiming the ORM handles negative slicing automatically is false, and on list-like semantics a negative start wraps from the end and returns unintended tail rows.

findings.title: Numeric cursor key used for datetime-ordered audit logs
findings.body: In src/sentry/api/paginator.py OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key does math.floor/ceil on getattr(item, self.key) and value_from_cursor returns the raw int cursor value. The only caller in src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py uses order_by='-datetime', so the key is a datetime object. math.floor(datetime) raises TypeError when building next/prev cursors, breaking page 2+ with a 500, and build_queryset would compare a datetime column to int 0/cursor value, causing a DB type error or wrong filtering and full scan.

findings.title: Forward negative offset silently clamped to zero
findings.body: In src/sentry/api/paginator.py BasePaginator.get_result now does start_offset = max(0, offset) for non-prev cursors instead of rejecting it. Every other offset-based paginator in the same file raises BadPaginationError (400) for offset < 0. Silently rewriting a corrupt/forged cursor to 0 returns the first page as if valid, causing duplicate pages and infinite client loops and hiding caller bugs, while the is_prev path still passes negative offsets through to Django slicing where they raise ValueError.

findings.title: Overly broad gate for unsafe pagination path
findings.body: In src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py the optimized/advanced pagination path is gated by request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access. has_global_access means access to all teams, not an admin/owner/audit role, and can be true for regular members. This exposes the negative-offset pagination path advertised as for authorized administrators to a much larger population than intended.
